claims.head: Special teams lean toward the Red Wings
claims.call: The Red Wings’ power play creates at least their usual 8.5 expected goals per 60.
claims.body: The Canadiens’ penalty kill is near the bottom of the league, and the Red Wings’ power play is one of the league’s best. Discipline matters more than usual for the Canadiens tonight.
claims.nums: Detroit 4th for power play (8.5 expected goals per 60) · Montréal 26th for penalty kill
claims.gist: The Red Wings’ power play has a soft target in the Canadiens’ kill.

check.rule: held if tonight's figure is at or above the team's usual level; partly if between the league average and that level; otherwise didn't happen

claims.head: The Red Wings give up good looks, and the Canadiens take them
claims.call: The Canadiens’ average shot has at least their usual 6.9% chance of going in.
claims.body: The Canadiens’ shots are some of the most dangerous in the league, and the Red Wings are near the bottom of the league at preventing dangerous ones. Look for plenty of good chances.
claims.nums: Montréal 2nd for shot quality (a 6.9% chance of scoring on the average shot) · Detroit 23rd for preventing dangerous shots
claims.gist: The Canadiens make their shots count, and the Red Wings allow dangerous ones.

notes.text: M. Kasper is out week to week and has missed the last 3 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters.
J. Compher is on injured reserve and has missed the last 2 games.
S. Edvinsson has not played this season. He is a top-pair defenseman. A. Johansson has taken his spot beside M. Seider.
O. Kapanen is day to day (lower body injury) and has not played this season. J. Slafkovský has taken his spot beside A. Newhook and I. Demidov.
K. Guhle is expected back after missing 4 games. Their recent numbers were built mostly without him.
A. Xhekaj has started killing penalties: on the ice for 27% of the team’s shorthanded time in 4 games, up from 6% last season.

MTL.head: The matchup suits Montréal
MTL.body: The two have been about even at controlling the play lately, Detroit will be without Kasper, Detroit is playing for the second night in a row, and Montréal has home ice. Detroit can make it interesting if their power play gets going.

DET.head: Not an easy night for Detroit
DET.body: The two have been about even at controlling the play lately, Detroit will be without Kasper, Detroit is playing for the second night in a row, and Montréal has home ice. Detroit can pull it off if their power play gets going.
